body:
Uh oh spaghettios.

I can confirm this issue is correct. I would recommend prioritizing this issue.
I'm surprised that `testonly` does not work at all..

My usecase is essentially what's in the `testonly` documentation: 

> This attribute is intended to mean that the target should not be contained in binaries that are released to production... rules that are dangerous to even link in, perhaps because they unconditionally override normal behavior, should definitely be marked testonly.

This bug report is a consequence of me discovering code that cleared databases (for tests) in production.

The advantage of `testonly` at the moment is that the `test` flag partitions all Bazel rules. If I wanted to use the constraint system, I would either have to mark all production or all testing rules appropriately. Perhaps `test = True` could put rules in an implicit environment.

Let's say I write a naïve HTTP server intended for development that's vulnerable to attacks like [slowloris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slowloris_%28computer_security%29), [billion laughs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billion_laughs), localhost:8000/../../../../etc/passwd, etc. I wouldn't normally be able to live with myself writing such a thing—unless I was able to guarantee it'll never end up in production. That's why I need `testonly`.

Otherwise we end up like Knight Capital, which lost almost half a billion dollars in forty-five minutes back on August 1st, 2012 because code that wasn't supposed to be in production suddenly activated.

Guaranteeing test code never ends up in production code also helps libraries and production binaries be less bloated.

I also believe that being able to the nature of sources and their relationships to each other at a very high level is what sets Bazel apart from many build systems. It's not so much about the logistics of building as it's about the definition, from which the build logistics are inferred. Definitions can also be bazel query'd. Looking at my notes file, I can see there have been situations in the past where I've written queries that look for `testonly`. So whatever we can do to help our build graph be better defined is a good thing IMHO. But definitions are only useful if the build system can guarantee they're correct and complete.

@jart: I mean the constraint system could be used to create a "test" environment that you could apply with "restricted_to".

Ok in the future we might want to migrate it to constraint system but let make it work for now. I'll try to put it in my queue. do not hesitate to ping if I forgot to update this bug with progress.
Having it be migrated to the constraint system would be acceptable to me.

Well because having a nice support with the constraint system is not going to happen soonish (this is doable right now but not built-in, so you have to mark all your test targets as "restricted_to"), we are going to fix testonly.
Awesome. I'm so happy to hear that Damien.
Ok I sent a fix for it :) It wasn't too hard. Might be in release 0.4 but it won't block it (meaning that if the CI is green tomorrow we will cut it without that change in).
You're amazing Damien. Thank you for fixing this important issue.
